diagrams.title: Approved deployment flow
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  U[GitHub collaborator] --> P[Prepare exact SHA and digest]
  P --> E[production Environment approval]
  E --> A[Deploy immutable outputs]
  A --> S[restricted SSH forced command]
  S --> H[server main SHA validation and build]
  H --> G[development runner guard]
  G --> R[atomic activation and runtime checks]

diagrams.title: Release activation state
diagrams.mermaid:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Requested
  Requested --> Rejected: invalid or non-main SHA
  Requested --> Built: isolated build passes
  Built --> Guarded: runner guard passes
  Guarded --> Active: restart and runtime checks pass
  Guarded --> RolledBack: activation check fails
  Active --> ActiveWithWarning: metadata prune fails

diagrams.title: Deployment trust boundaries
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  C[GitHub collaborator] -->|workflow dispatch| P[Prepare immutable SHA and digest]
  P -->|exact outputs| E[production Environment]
  E -->|required reviewer approval| A[Deploy job]
  A -->|full SHA and pinned host key| F[restricted SSH forced command]
  F -->|validated SHA and digest argv| D[root deploy script]
  D -->|main ancestry verified| R[single-use release]
  X[Arbitrary command or malformed SHA] -->|reject| F
  Y[Main-external commit] -->|reject| D
  Z[Activation failure] -->|restore previous pointer| K[known-good release]
  P -. no secrets .-> S[runtime secrets]
  C -. no shell .-> D

clauses.statement: The manual deployment workflow resolves an omitted input to origin/main and accepts an explicit input only when it is a full 40-character commit SHA reachable from origin/main.

A secretless prepare job resolves and displays immutable target and control-plane outputs before approval; the production Environment deployment job depends only on those outputs, performs no checkout or target resolution after approval, and uses read-only repository permissions, non-cancelling concurrency, pinned host keys, and a commit-pinned checkout action in prepare.

The dedicated SSH principal accepts only deploy followed by one full hexadecimal SHA and one control-plane SHA-256 digest, rejects an installed-script digest mismatch before build, and passes the SHA and digest as separate arguments to the root-owned deploy script.
The server independently fetches origin/main and rejects a requested commit that is not reachable from origin/main before creating or activating a release.

Given a valid unbuilt commit, the server builds the Lightsail runtime's workspace dependencies and application packages in a detached release worktree and changes the active symlink only after the Jimmy entrypoint exists.

test_refs.case: Jimmy build failure propagation fixture passed

clauses.statement: Every service restart waits for the installed development-runner guard and fails without switching the running service when the guard times out.

test_refs.case: deploy script, workflow contract, and rollback validation passed

clauses.statement: Given activation or systemd active-check failure and an existing previous release, the deploy script restores the previous symlink and restarts the service before returning failure.

test_refs.case: deploy script, workflow contract, and rollback validation passed

clauses.statement: The repository and deployment output contain no SSH private key, runtime token, gateway environment value, or disabled host-key checking configuration.

A successful workflow reports server-side build, guarded restart, systemd active evidence, control-plane digest, MainPID, and resolved release entrypoint without claiming Slack or Web release outcome completion.
The deploy-script test rejects arbitrary SSH commands and short SHAs, verifies shell syntax, parses the workflow contract, and exercises rollback pointer restoration.

test_refs.case: deploy script, workflow contract, and rollback validation passed

clauses.statement: After a successful activation, worktree metadata pruning failure emits a warning but does not reverse deployment success.

test_refs.case: deploy script, workflow contract, and rollback validation passed

clauses.statement: Reinstalling the control plane preserves an existing active release pointer and seeds it from the source clone only on first installation; application rollback uses the current workflow control plane independently of the target application SHA and never runs an installer from the rollback target.
